question: What did Kestrel Robotics say about Tray.io?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every statement made about Tray.io (also written Tray), including comparisons to OrbitFlow, reasons given for considering or rejecting it, and any pricing, features or experience the speaker mentions.
assumptions: Question refers to the Kestrel Robotics call (CALL-020); Tray.io is treated as a competitor mentioned in the call.
Tray.io and Tray are treated as the same product.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: We're three weeks into evaluating Tray.io.
findings.context: Kestrel is three weeks into evaluating Tray.io. — Customer states the current evaluation status of Tray.io.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Well. Genuinely well. Their team's been good.
findings.context: Tray.io's evaluation is going well and Tray's team has been good. — Asked how the Tray evaluation is going.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: Tray don't have a connector and we're looking at building against its API
findings.context: Tray.io does not have a connector for Kestrel's mid-market manufacturing ERP, so Kestrel would need to build against its API. — Customer identifies the ERP integration gap as the one issue in the Tray evaluation.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: I'm not going to tell you Tray is bad. It isn't. We lose to them and we beat them and it usually comes down to fit rather than quality.
findings.context: OrbitFlow's vendor view is that Tray is a good product, not bad, and that losses against Tray usually come down to fit rather than quality. — OrbitFlow rep discussing Tray in a competitive context.

findings.speaker: Rafael Santos
findings.quote: We've got a decision date and I'm not moving it.
findings.context: Kestrel has a decision date for choosing a vendor in mid-October, and will not restart the evaluation (which includes Tray). — Customer on timing of the Tray decision.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Run it against Tray — I mean that, run it against Tray, you're three weeks in and it costs you nothing.
findings.context: OrbitFlow rep suggests Kestrel run the operations-can-change-it test against Tray, and says if Tray passes, Kestrel should buy Tray. — OrbitFlow rep recommending a competitor's product as a test.

draft.answer: Kestrel Robotics' COO Rafael Santos said Kestrel is three weeks into evaluating Tray.io and that it is going well, with a good Tray team [C1][C2]. The one issue he named was that Tray has no connector for Kestrel's mid-market manufacturing ERP, so Kestrel is looking at building against its API [C3]. Kestrel has a mid-October decision date that Santos said he won't move [C4].

claims.text: Rafael Santos (COO, Kestrel Robotics) said Kestrel is three weeks into evaluating Tray.io, and that the evaluation is going 'genuinely well' with a good Tray team.
Santos said Tray does not have a connector for Kestrel's mid-market manufacturing ERP, and Kestrel is looking at building against its API; he presented this as the issue in the Tray evaluation.
Santos said Kestrel has a decision date (mid-October per the finding) and he is not moving it; the evaluation, which includes Tray, will not restart.

not_covered: Pricing, features, or other Tray.io details beyond the ERP connector gap were not stated by Kestrel in the findings.
Which other vendors are in Kestrel's evaluation is not covered.
